title: A Last Chance to Avert Climate Disaster?

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日时事通讯 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访一些商业、政治和文化领域举足轻重的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我们将在 NYTimes.com 上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》

sentences.en: Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: App 进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收听。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 我是今天的主持人。

sentences.en: Hundreds of heads of state have gathered in Scotland for what they say may be their last real chance to avoid a climate disaster.
sentences.zh: 数百位国家元首聚集在苏格兰，参加他们所说可能是避免气候灾难的最后一次真正机会的会议。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Samini Sengupta, about whether they're right, and if global climate talks like these ever really accomplish anything.
sentences.zh: 我与我的同事萨米尼·森古普塔谈论了他们是否正确，以及像这样全球气候会谈是否真的能达成任何成果。

sentences.en: Hey, Samini.
sentences.zh: 嘿，萨米尼。

sentences.en: I was rushing from one end of this giant conference center to this quiet corner where
sentences.zh: 我正从这个巨大会议中心的一头匆忙赶往我所在的这个安静角落，

sentences.en: I'm at, and I got stuck in a scrum with, I think, John Kerry coming out.
sentences.zh: 然后我卷入了一群人里，我想，那是约翰·克瑞刚出来的时候。

sentences.en: And then I got stuck in another scrum with, I think it was Prince Charles, but I'm not really sure.
sentences.zh: 接着我又卷入了另一群人里，我想那是查尔斯王子，但我其实不太确定。

sentences.en: That's a heck of a set of scruMs. And me trying to squeeze in between.
sentences.zh: 那可真是一群接一群的人潮。而我正努力从中间挤过去。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: The adventures of climate reporting.
sentences.zh: 气候报道的奇遇记。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So Samini, I wonder if you could just describe exactly where you are and what you're seeing all around you.
sentences.zh: 那么萨米尼，我想请你描述一下你究竟在哪里，以及你周围看到了什么。

sentences.en: So I'm in a giant conference center in Glasgow, officially called the Conference of
sentences.zh: 我现在身处格拉斯哥的一个巨大会议中心，官方名称是联合国气候变化框架公约締約方

sentences.en: Parties to the United Nations Climate Change Convention.
sentences.zh: 大会。

sentences.en: So it's called COP26 for short.
sentences.zh: 所以简称 COP26。

sentences.en: This is the 26th such session.
sentences.zh: 这是第 26 届此类会议。

sentences.en: There are plenary halls where the leaders are giving their speeches.
sentences.zh: 这里有全体会议大厅，领导人们在里面发表演讲。

sentences.en: There is a pavilion where every country can set up its own pavilion.
sentences.zh: 这里还有一个展馆区，每个国家都可以设立自己的展馆。

sentences.en: And the one from Tuvalu, which is a Pacific Island nation, I just walked past it this afternoon, and they have these life-sized polar bears in life jackets.
sentences.zh: 图瓦卢是一个太平洋岛国，我今天下午刚路过他们的展馆，他们那里有穿着救生衣的真人大小北极熊。

sentences.en: It's become quite a spot for selfies.
sentences.zh: 这里已经成了自拍的热门地点。

sentences.en: I think we have to comment on the metaphorical intent of that.
sentences.zh: 我想我们必须评论一下这其中的隐喻意图。

sentences.en: I believe the metaphorical intent is that the ice is melting.
sentences.zh: 我相信其隐喻意图是冰正在融化。

sentences.en: The polar bears need to be rescued.
sentences.zh: 北极熊需要被拯救。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's also a little penguin hanging from a noose above the polar bears.
sentences.zh: 在北极熊上方的绞索上还挂着一只小企鹅。

sentences.en: Ooh, a darker metaphor.
sentences.zh: 哦，一个更黑暗的隐喻。

sentences.en: Yeah, pretty grim.
sentences.zh: 是的，相当严峻。

sentences.en: Rumors have spread that Australia, the Australian pavilion, is serving free coffee.
sentences.zh: 有传言说澳大利亚，也就是澳大利亚展馆，在供应免费咖啡。

sentences.en: So there's quite a long line there today.
sentences.zh: 所以今天那里排起了相当长的队伍。

sentences.en: So that's kind of what it looks like.
sentences.zh: 这就是那里的样子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Well, as I think those dark scenes you just described hint at, we are at a moment when the climate is in crisis.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你刚才描述的那些黑暗场景所暗示的，我们正处于一个气候处于危机的时刻。

sentences.en: And despite years and years and years of global talks, despite treaties like the
sentences.zh: 尽管经历了年复一年、漫长而又漫长的全球会谈，尽管有源自这些会谈的《巴黎协定》等气候变化条约，

sentences.en: Paris Agreement on climate change that come from those talks, carbon emissions have gotten worse, not better.
sentences.zh: 但碳排放情况非但没有改善，反而恶化了。

sentences.en: And extreme climate events are becoming even more destructive, not less.
sentences.zh: 极端气候事件也变得更具破坏性，而不是相反。

sentences.en: And so I think the question for many people is, what exactly is the point of a conference like this?
sentences.zh: 因此，我想对许多人来说，问题在于，像这样的一场会议究竟有什么意义？

sentences.en: Haven't we learned that these global climate talks are not really an effective way to solve the climate problem?
sentences.zh: 难道我们还没有明白，这些全球气候会谈并不是解决气候问题的真正有效途径吗？

sentences.en: And I wonder if you can engage in that skepticism for a moment, that these conferences can seem like a lot of pomp and circumstance and empty promises.
sentences.zh: 我想请你暂时体会一下这种怀疑态度，即这些会议看起来可能充满了浮华、礼仪和空洞的承诺。

sentences.en: There are some who would look at these climate summits and say, look, you come together every year and you all make speeches and you promise various things.
sentences.zh: 有些人看待这些气候峰会时会说，看呐，你们每年聚在一起，发表各种演讲，许下各种承诺。

sentences.en: They are all voluntary.
sentences.zh: 这些全都是自愿的。

sentences.en: They are not binding.
sentences.zh: 它们不具约束力。

sentences.en: And in the end, you are not doing what the science demands, which is to pivot really quickly away from burning coal, oil and gas to limit the rise in global average temperatures.
sentences.zh: 到头来，你们并没有做到科学所要求的事情，也就是真正迅速地从燃烧煤炭、石油和天然气转向限制全球平均气温上升。

sentences.en: And so, you know, the frustration that you hear is this is all a bunch of talk and there's not enough action.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你听到的沮丧情绪是，这一切都只是一堆空谈，而缺乏足够的行动。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And what's the optimist's case, the argument for seeing a conference like this as important, as meaningful, and ultimately impactful?
sentences.zh: 那么乐观主义者的看法是什么？将这样一场会议视为重要、有意义且最终产生影响的理由是什么？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So another way of asking that is, you know, why bother when things are so bad?
sentences.zh: 换一种方式来问就是，你知道，既然情况这么糟，为什么还要费劲呢？

sentences.en: Well, the argument you will often hear is precisely because things are bad and they could be much worse is why you need a summit like this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你经常听到的论点恰恰是：正因为情况糟糕，而且还可能变得更糟，所以才需要这样一场峰会。

sentences.en: The future is not pre-written.
sentences.zh: 未来并非预先写好的。

sentences.en: It's up to the big, powerful countries that are gathered here to determine what kind of future is going to be most likely.
sentences.zh: 这取决于聚集在这里的大国和强国，来决定哪种未来最有可能实现。

sentences.en: The point of this summit is for the leaders of this big, polluter countries and for everyone else
sentences.zh: 这次峰会的意义在于，让这些排放大国的领导人以及受气候变化影响的每一个人

sentences.en: who's affected by climate change to gather in one place to nudge each other to do better and to hold each other to account.
sentences.zh: 聚集在一个地方，互相敦促做得更好，并让彼此承担责任。

sentences.en: The whole thing is built on this system of diplomatic peer pressure.
sentences.zh: 整个事情都建立在这种外交同侪压力系统之上。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So with that in mind, these two arguments about this conference, what has actually happened at this conference so far?
sentences.zh: 那么，带着这两种关于这次会议的争论，到目前为止，这次会议实际发生了什么？

sentences.en: I know we're just a few days into it, but they've been meaningful days.
sentences.zh: 我知道会议才开始几天，但这些天很有意义。

sentences.en: So the conference began Sunday.
sentences.zh: 会议于周日开幕。

sentences.en: And in a way, the conference really began with this other meeting, which happened in Rome.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，会议真正开始于在罗马举行的另一场会议。

sentences.en: And that's where the world's 20 biggest economies, the G20, which are also the 20 biggest polluters, were meeting.
sentences.zh: 那是全球二十大经济体（G20）开会的地方，它们也是全球二十大污染国。

sentences.en: And they were trying to come to an agreement on what they're willing to do to address climate change.
sentences.zh: 他们试图就愿意采取什么行动来应对气候变化达成一致。

sentences.en: And they actually took some incremental steps.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上采取了一些渐进式的步骤。

sentences.en: Probably key among them was that they agreed to, quote unquote, pursue efforts to keep a very key temperature threshold within reach.
sentences.zh: 其中最关键的可能是，他们同意“致力于努力”将一个非常关键的温控阈值保持在触手可及的范围内。

sentences.en: And that threshold is to limit the average global temperature rise to within 1.5 degrees Celsius between pre-industrial times and the end of this century.
sentences.zh: 这个阈值是将本世纪末与工业化前时期相比的全球平均气温升幅限制在 1.5 摄氏度以内。

sentences.en: And why does that pledge matter so much?
sentences.zh: 为什么这个承诺如此重要？

sentences.en: Because that feels like a familiar pledge.
sentences.zh: 因为这听起来是一个熟悉的承诺。

sentences.en: Well, that is one of the goals of the Paris Agreement.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是《巴黎协定》的目标之一。

sentences.en: It is increasingly an important north star because after you get past 1.5 degrees, the likelihood of the really, really bad stuff goes up significantly.
sentences.zh: 它越来越成为一颗重要的北极星，因为一旦超过 1.5 度，发生非常非常糟糕的事情的可能性就会显著上升。

sentences.en: That's the scientific consensus.
sentences.zh: 这是科学界的共识。

sentences.en: And right now, by the way, we are on track to rise by about 3 degrees Celsius.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，目前我们的气温上升轨迹大约是 3 摄氏度。

sentences.en: So after this meeting in Rome, where they commit themselves to 1.5, they all fly from Italy to Glasgow.
sentences.zh: 因此，在罗马会议上承诺将升温控制在 1.5 度之后，他们都从意大利飞往格拉斯哥。

sentences.en: You can shove your climate crisis up your arse.
sentences.zh: 你可以把你们的气候危机塞进你们的屁眼里。

sentences.en: You can shove your climate crisis up your arse.
sentences.zh: 你可以把你们的气候危机塞进你们的屁眼里。

sentences.en: By the time they reach, there are protesters greeting them, essentially saying that they are doing a lot of talking and not a lot of doing.
sentences.zh: 当他们抵达时，抗议者迎面而来，基本上是在说他们光说不练。

sentences.en: And Greta Thunberg, among others, are leading chants saying,
sentences.zh: 格蕾塔·通贝里等人正带领着口号，高呼：

sentences.en: No more blah, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 不要再废话了，废话，废话，废话。

sentences.en: Enough of this blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 受够了这些废话。

sentences.en: She's making the skeptics case for this conference.
sentences.zh: 她正在为这场会议的怀疑论者提供论据。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So then the summit begins with speeches.
sentences.zh: 于是峰会在演讲中拉开帷幕。

sentences.en: It's time to say, enough.
sentences.zh: 是时候说：够了。

sentences.en: Enough of brutalizing biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 停止对生物多样性的残酷摧残。

sentences.en: Enough of killing ourselves with carbon.
sentences.zh: 停止用碳杀死我们自己。

sentences.en: Enough of treating nature like a toilet.
sentences.zh: 停止把大自然当成厕所。

sentences.en: The Secretary General of the United Nations, Antonio Guterres, makes a powerful case.
sentences.zh: 联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯发表了强有力的陈词。

sentences.en: Enough of burning and drilling and mining our way deeper.
sentences.zh: 停止通过燃烧、钻探和采矿让我们越陷越深。

sentences.en: We are digging our own graves.
sentences.zh: 我们正在自掘坟墓。

sentences.en: He says we are digging our own grave by continuing to drill for oil and gas and coal.
sentences.zh: 他说，通过继续开采石油、天然气和煤炭，我们正在自掘坟墓。

sentences.en: I urge you, choose ambition.
sentences.zh: 我敦促你们，选择雄心。

sentences.en: Choose solidarity.
sentences.zh: 选择团结。

sentences.en: Choose to safeguard our future and save humanity.
sentences.zh: 选择守护我们的未来并拯救人类。

sentences.en: And I thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: Good afternoon, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家下午好。

sentences.en: Welcome to COP.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到 COP 大会。

sentences.en: Boris Johnson, the Prime Minister of Britain, which is the host country.
sentences.zh: 说话的是作为主办国英国首相的鲍里斯·约翰逊。

sentences.en: Welcome to Glasgow and to Scotland, whose most globally famous fictional son is almost certainly a man
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到格拉斯哥和苏格兰，这里全球最著名的虚构之子几乎可以肯定是一个名叫

sentences.en: called James Bond, who generally comes to the climax of his highly lucrative films strapped to a doomsday device.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·邦德的人，他那些利润丰厚的电影的高潮通常都是被绑在末日装置上。

sentences.en: He begins his speech with an analogy of James Bond and a clicking time bomb.
sentences.zh: 他的演讲以詹姆斯·邦德和滴答作响的定时炸弹的类比开场。

sentences.en: We are in roughly the same position, my fellow global leaders, as James Bond today.
sentences.zh: 各位全球领导人同仁，我们今天所处的位置与詹姆斯·邦德大致相同。

sentences.en: Except that the tragedy is this is not a movie and the doomsday device is real.
sentences.zh: 唯一的悲剧在于，这不是电影，末日装置是真实存在的。

sentences.en: And then.
sentences.zh: 然后。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们。

sentences.en: Joe Biden appears on the podium.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登登上了演讲台。

sentences.en: My Build Back Better framework will make historic investments in clean energy.
sentences.zh: 我的“重建美好”框架将对清洁能源进行历史性的投资。

sentences.en: The most significant investment to deal with the climate crisis that any advanced nation has made ever.
sentences.zh: 这是任何发达国家有史以来为应对气候危机做出的最大投资。

sentences.en: And this is, of course, the reentry of the United States into the Paris Agreement after President Trump pulled the country out of the Paris Agreement.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是在特朗普总统让美国退出《巴黎协定》之后，美国重新加入《巴黎协定》。

sentences.en: And we have to help much more than we have thus far.
sentences.zh: 我们必须提供比迄今为止更多的帮助。

sentences.en: God bless you all and may God save the planet.
sentences.zh: 愿上帝保佑你们所有人，愿上帝拯救地球。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We also hear from small and very, very vulnerable countries.
sentences.zh: 我们还听取了小型且非常、非常脆弱的国家的发言。

sentences.en: Your Royal Highness, Excellencies, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen.
sentences.zh: 尊敬的王室殿下、各位大使、各位杰出的来宾、女士们先生们。

sentences.en: The Prime Minister of Barbados, Mia Motley, says...
sentences.zh: 巴巴多斯总理米娅·莫特利表示……

sentences.en: The pandemic has taught us that national solutions to global problems do not work.
sentences.zh: 大流行病教会了我们，针对全球问题的国家级解决方案是行不通的。

sentences.en: This is the moment for leaders of big countries to lead.
sentences.zh: 现在是大国领导人展现领导力的时候了。

sentences.en: Do some leaders in this world believe that they can survive and thrive on their own?
sentences.zh: 难道这个世界上的一些领导人认为他们可以靠自己生存和繁荣吗？

sentences.en: Have they not learnt from the pandemic?
sentences.zh: 他们难道没有从大流行病中吸取教训吗？

sentences.en: Can there be peace and prosperity if one third of the world literally prospers and the other two thirds of the world live under siege and face calamitous threats?
sentences.zh: 如果世界上三分之一的人口 literalmente（字面意思上）繁荣昌盛，而另外三分之二的人口生活在围困中并面临灾难性的威胁，还能有和平与繁荣吗？

sentences.en: As I speak, Your Excellencies, our global canoe is headed for storms that will sink us while sea water pours the boat through massive gaps.
sentences.zh: 在我发言时，尊敬的各位大使，我们的全球独木舟正驶向会让我们沉没的风暴，而海水正通过巨大的缝隙涌入船内。

sentences.en: You also hear from the leader of Fiji, Frank Vainamarama.
sentences.zh: 你还会听到斐济领导人弗兰克·姆拜尼马拉马的发言。

sentences.en: He said the existence of countries like his, low-lying Pacific Island nations, are not negotiable.
sentences.zh: 他说，像他这样的国家，即低洼的太平洋岛国，其生存是不可谈判的。

sentences.en: To all leaders here, the message of the Pacific is simple.
sentences.zh: 对于这里的所有领导人，来自太平洋的信息很简单。

sentences.en: Our canoe is sinking.
sentences.zh: 我们的独木舟正在下沉。

sentences.en: Pick up your buckets and start bailing now before it's too late.
sentences.zh: 拿起你们的桶，现在就开始舀水，免得为时已晚。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And these are really reminders to everyone else in the hall about what's at stake.
sentences.zh: 这些真的是在提醒大厅里的其他所有人，什么才是生死攸关的大事。

sentences.en: Honorable guests, this brings us to the end of our national statements.
sentences.zh: 尊敬的来宾们，这标志着我们国家发言的结束。

sentences.en: And what are you thinking as you're watching these speeches, especially from the smaller island countries?
sentences.zh: 当你观看这些演讲时，尤其是来自较小岛国的演讲，你在想什么？

sentences.en: I mean, I've covered several international summits convened by the United Nations, like this one.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我报道过几次由联合国召集的国际峰会，就像这次一样。

sentences.en: And it strikes me every time that this is where countries, big and small, rich and poor, powerful and almost never heard from,
sentences.zh: 每一次都让我印象深刻的是，正是在这里，无论国家大小、贫富、强大与否，还是那些几乎从未被听到的声音——

sentences.en: if you are in the U.S., they all get the same airtime.
sentences.zh: 如果你在美国，他们都会得到相同的播出时间。

sentences.en: They all stand at the same podium.
sentences.zh: 他们都站在同一个讲台上。

sentences.en: They negotiate with each other.
sentences.zh: 他们彼此谈判。

sentences.en: It is the ultimate platform for global collective action.
sentences.zh: 这是全球集体行动的终极平台。

sentences.en: And in this case, on a really, really big and high-stakes global problem.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，是针对一个非常、非常巨大且风险极高的全球问题。

sentences.en: So this would be another argument for the optimist's version of why these conferences matter?
sentences.zh: 所以，这会是支持乐观主义者关于为什么这些会议重要的版本的另一个论点吗？

sentences.en: As a realist, I can tell you that a summit like this is where the Davids and the Goliaths in the world,
sentences.zh: 作为一个现实主义者，我可以告诉你，像这样的峰会是世界上的大卫和歌利亚们——

sentences.en: you know, among nations, they sit at the same table, they egg each other on, they pressure each other.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在各个国家之间，他们坐在同一张桌子旁，互相激励，互相施压。

sentences.en: It's not a one-way street.
sentences.zh: 这不是单向的。

sentences.en: It's not the powerful, pressing, only, small, vulnerable countries.
sentences.zh: 这不是那些强大、紧迫、仅有的、弱小的脆弱国家。

sentences.en: It's also the other way around.
sentences.zh: 情况也是反过来的。

sentences.en: And it's where the leader of really powerful, big, rich countries like Germany or the United States
sentences.zh: 这也是像德国或美国这样真正强大、大型、富裕国家的领导人

sentences.en: have to hear the leader of Fiji or the leader of Barbados.
sentences.zh: 不得不倾听斐济领导人或巴巴多斯领导人意见的地方。

sentences.en: Tell them, this is your moment to lead.
sentences.zh: 告诉他们，这是你们发挥领导作用的时刻。

sentences.en: Or blame them for things that have gone terribly wrong.
sentences.zh: 或者因为搞得一团糟而指责他们。

sentences.en: That too.
sentences.zh: 这也是其中之一。

sentences.en: But of course, the big question is, are those large, wealthy nations going to actually act?
sentences.zh: 但当然，最大的问题是，这些大型富裕国家真的会采取行动吗？

sentences.en: Are they going to make commitments and keep them in ways that benefit those small, vulnerable countries?
sentences.zh: 他们会做出承诺并兑现这些承诺，从而让那些弱小的脆弱国家受益吗？

sentences.en: Precisely.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶唱片时代去夜店当DJ的时候，每晚你都要带着300件你最珍贵的财产去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 然后你把一个DJ台变成了一个像是由美丽的50年历史艺术品组成的、活生生的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today, and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 订阅《纽约时报》，立即下载时报应用程序，即可免费访问30天。

sentences.en: So, Sumini, what kind of commitments and pledges are actually made at this conference?
sentences.zh: 那么，苏米尼，这次会议究竟做出了什么样的承诺和保证？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, has this summit produced in the first three days a coherent global plan to exit fossil fuel extraction and use?
sentences.zh: 那么，在头三天里，这次峰会是否产生了一个连贯的全球计划，以退出化石燃料的开采和使用？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: But have there been significant steps announced in these last couple of days?
sentences.zh: 但在过去这两天里，是否宣布了重大的步骤？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: First, the United States has led this effort to persuade something around 90 countries to sign on to a pledge, again, a voluntary pledge, to cut methane emissions by 30% by 2030.
sentences.zh: 首先，美国带头争取了大约90个国家签署一项承诺，再次强调，这是一项自愿承诺，即到2030年将甲烷排放量减少30%。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And why does that matter?
sentences.zh: 为什么这很重要？

sentences.en: How big a deal is it?
sentences.zh: 这有多大不了的？

sentences.en: It matters because methane warms the atmosphere super faSt.
sentences.zh: 这很重要，因为甲烷使大气变暖的速度超级快。

sentences.en: It's produced in oil and gas operations, in trash landfills, and all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 它产生于石油和天然气开采、垃圾填埋场以及各种各样的活动中。

sentences.en: Now, we'll have to see how countries fulfill that pledge.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们还得看各国如何兑现这一承诺。

sentences.en: They're going to have to go back and change their rules and regulations, or maybe there are laws to actually reduce their methane emissions.
sentences.zh: 他们将不得不回国修改规则和条例，或者制定法律来真正减少他们的甲烷排放。

sentences.en: And notably, there are a lot of key countries that are not on board with this so-called global methane pledge.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，有许多关键国家并未加入这个所谓的全球甲烷承诺。

sentences.en: Like?
sentences.zh: 比如？

sentences.en: So, Russia is not on board, a major oil and gas producer, nor is China, nor India, nor Australia.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯没有加入，它是一个主要的油气生产国；中国也没有加入，印度和澳大利亚也没有。

sentences.en: Those are some pretty big gaps in that agreement.
sentences.zh: 该协议中存在一些相当大的漏洞。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, some pretty big gaps there.
sentences.zh: 所以，那里有一些相当大的漏洞。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: What else?
sentences.zh: 还有什么？

sentences.en: The other big global accord that we heard about today was a commitment to end deforestation by 2030.
sentences.zh: 我们今天听到的另一个重大全球协定是承诺在2030年前结束毁林行为。

sentences.en: So, about 100 countries signed on to this.
sentences.zh: 因此，大约有100个国家签署了这项协议。

sentences.en: It includes Brazil, which, of course, contains a big chunk of the Amazon, the lungs of the planet.
sentences.zh: 其中包括巴西，当然，巴西拥有亚马逊的大部分地区，那是地球之肺。

sentences.en: It includes Russia, which has, you know, some really important big boreal forests.
sentences.zh: 其中包括俄罗斯，你知道，它拥有一些非常重要的大片北方针叶林。

sentences.en: It includes China.
sentences.zh: 其中包括中国。

sentences.en: But this is all a bit of a deja vu, because in 2014, world leaders promised to reduce deforestation by half by now.
sentences.zh: 但这有点像似曾相识，因为在2014年，世界领导人曾承诺到目前将毁林面积减少一半。

sentences.en: And they promised to eliminate deforestation entirely by 2030, which is exactly what the accord announced today says.
sentences.zh: 他们还承诺在2030年前彻底消除毁林现象，这与今天宣布的协定完全一致。

sentences.en: In fact, since that pledge, deforestation actually accelerated.
sentences.zh: 事实上，自从该承诺做出以来，毁林速度反而加快了。

sentences.en: So, you know, let's see if, second time around, world leaders will actually keep their promise.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，让我们看看第二次世界大战时世界领导人是否会真正兑现他们的承诺。

sentences.en: So, in theory, we should be quite skeptical of this pledge, because this pledge was made in the past and not kept.
sentences.zh: 因此，理论上我们应该对这一承诺持相当怀疑的态度，因为这个承诺过去曾做出过却没有兑现。

sentences.en: In theory, we should be skeptical of all pledges, because all pledges are voluntary, and what matters is how they achieve those pledges.
sentences.zh: 理论上，我们应该对所有的承诺持怀疑态度，因为所有的承诺都是自愿的，真正重要的是他们如何兑现这些承诺。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, Sumini, taken together, if kept, how would these two pledges, on methane and on deforestation,
sentences.zh: 那么，苏米尼，综合来看，如果得以兑现，关于甲烷和毁林的这两项承诺，

sentences.en: how much progress would that represent when it comes to 1.5 degrees and keeping warming beneath that threshold?
sentences.zh: 在将温升控制在1.5度及这一阈值以下方面，将代表多大的进展？

sentences.en: Both the methane pledge and the deforestation pledge are significant, but taken together, they are not going to be sufficient to reach the 1.5 threshold.
sentences.zh: 甲烷承诺和毁林承诺都很重要，但综合起来，它们还不足以达到1.5度的阈值。

sentences.en: Okay, so those are multi-country agreements.
sentences.zh: 好的，这些是多国协议。

sentences.en: What about individual countries?
sentences.zh: 那单个国家呢？

sentences.en: What kind of pledges and promises did they make relating to 1.5 degrees?
sentences.zh: 他们做出了哪些关于1.5度的承诺和保证？

sentences.en: There were two significant individual country pledges.
sentences.zh: 有两个重要的单一国家承诺。

sentences.en: The first one came from the Indian Prime Minister, Narendra Modi.
sentences.zh: 第一个来自印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪。

sentences.en: He said India would significantly ramp up renewable energy production, and that by 2030, 50% of its energy mix would come from renewable energy.
sentences.zh: 他说，印度将大幅提高可再生能源产量，到2030年，其能源结构中将有50%来自可再生能源。

sentences.en: This was rather vague with very few specifics, and there was a lot of head-scratching,
sentences.zh: 这相当含糊，细节很少，让人摸不着头脑，

sentences.en: but still a significant commitment by a big emerging economy to ramp up renewable energy sources.
sentences.zh: 但对于一个扩大可再生能源来源的大型新兴经济体来说，这仍然是一个重大的承诺。

sentences.en: He did not, however, say anything about the main source of electricity in India, which is burning coal, and he didn't say anything about India's coal use.
sentences.zh: 然而，他没有提及印度电力主要来源即燃煤发电的任何情况，也没有提及印度的煤炭使用情况。

sentences.en: However, on Tuesday from South Africa came a very important announcement about that.
sentences.zh: 不过，周二来自南非的一个非常重要的声明涉及到了这一点。

sentences.en: South Africa said that it would begin to plot its exit from coal, and it announced a sort of transition plan.
sentences.zh: 南非表示，它将开始规划退出煤炭，并宣布了一种转型计划。

sentences.en: The reason why this is important is that South Africa is the first big emerging economy to say, yep, we're going to exit coal, and this is how we're going to do it.
sentences.zh: 这之所以重要，是因为南非是第一个表示“是的，我们要退出煤炭，这就是我们要做的方式”的大型新兴经济体。

sentences.en: And this commitment could send a very important signal to other emerging economies about how an exit from coal can actually happen.
sentences.zh: 这一承诺可能会向其他新兴经济体发出一个非常重要的信号，即如何切实实现退出煤炭。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Okay, well, what about China, the United States, and Russia, three of the world's largest and biggest pooliers?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么中国、美国和俄罗斯这三个世界最大、污染最严重的国家呢？

sentences.en: Did they make any meaningful pledges here?
sentences.zh: 他们在这里做出任何有意义的承诺了吗？

sentences.en: The United States had already said, early on this year, soon after President Biden took office, it announced its national climate plan or its climate goal.
sentences.zh: 美国今年早些时候，即拜登总统上任后不久，就已经宣布了其国家气候计划或气候目标。

sentences.en: And in it, the United States said it would reduce by about 50% its emissions by 2030 compared to the emissions levels in 2005.
sentences.zh: 在其中，美国表示，与2005年的排放水平相比，到2030年将其排放量减少约50%。

sentences.en: That's pretty ambitious.
sentences.zh: 这相当雄心勃勃。

sentences.en: The big question, of course, is how is this administration going to deliver that target,
sentences.zh: 当然，最大的问题是，考虑到该届政府在国会关于其主要气候立法方面仍然面临相当大的阻力，它将如何实现这一目标？

sentences.en: given that it faces some pretty significant opposition still in Congress on its kind of main climate legislation?
sentences.zh: 考虑到它在国会的气候主要立法上仍然面临相当大的反对阻力？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay, what about China and what about Russia?
sentences.zh: 好的，那中国和俄罗斯呢？

sentences.en: China, too, has already said that it would stop funding coal-fired power plants overseas,
sentences.zh: 中国也已经表示将停止在海外资助燃煤电厂，

sentences.en: which is a big deal because China is the biggest funder of coal-fired power plants overseas.
sentences.zh: 这是一件大事，因为中国是海外燃煤电厂的最大出资国。

sentences.en: However, China has said nothing so far about when it plans to get out of coal at home.
sentences.zh: 然而，中国迄今为止并未透露何时计划在本土摆脱煤炭。

sentences.en: It consumes by far the largest share of coal anywhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 它消耗了全球绝大部分的煤炭。

sentences.en: And China's updated climate plan is not that different from its original climate plan, which is that China will continue to grow its greenhouse gas emissions until 2030.
sentences.zh: 中国更新后的气候计划与其最初的气候计划没有太大区别，即中国将继续增加温室气体排放，直到2030年。

sentences.en: That's China.
sentences.zh: 这就是中国。

sentences.en: Russia has announced a rather vague net zero target by 2060.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯则宣布了一个相当含糊的净零排放目标，时间定在2060年。

sentences.en: But, of course, Russia has no plans at all to rein in the extraction of oil and gas from its territory.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，俄罗斯根本没有计划限制其领土内的石油和天然气开采。

sentences.en: So when we think of the biggest polluters, the countries that so many of these smaller countries like Barbados and Fiji are looking to for leadership,
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们想到最大的污染国，即巴巴多斯和斐济等许多较小国家寄予厚望的国家，

sentences.en: pleading to for leadership at this conference,
sentences.zh: 在这个会议上恳求他们发挥领导作用时，

sentences.en: how should we be thinking about the impressiveness or ambition of these commitments?
sentences.zh: 我们应该如何看待这些承诺的亮眼程度或雄心壮志？

sentences.en: They don't seem that impressive or ambitious in their details.
sentences.zh: 从细节上看，它们似乎并不那么亮眼或雄心勃勃。

sentences.en: Well, in reality, they are nowhere close to the 1.5-degree target.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现实中，它们距离1.5度的目标还相去甚远。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So does that mean that this peer pressure model, the purpose of these conferences, is failing?
sentences.zh: 那么这是否意味着这种同伴压力模式，即这些会议的目的，正在失效？

sentences.en: Is this the skeptics' version, you know, of a conference coming to pass?
sentences.zh: 这难道就是怀疑论者眼中那种流于形式的会议吗？

sentences.en: Well, let's truth squad this for a minute, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们花点时间来核查一下真相，好吗？

sentences.en: Please.
sentences.zh: 请吧。

sentences.en: Let's do a thought experiment and say, well, what if there was no Paris Agreement?
sentences.zh: 让我们做一个思想实验，假设，如果没有《巴黎协定》会怎样？

sentences.en: And there was no diplomatic forum like this where countries nudge each other to set better climate targets
sentences.zh: 如果没有这样一个外交论坛，让各国互相敦促以设定更好的气候目标，

sentences.en: and report back and, you know, submit all this data that journalists like us can study and hold their feet to the fire.
sentences.zh: 并汇报情况，提交所有这些数据，以便像我们这样的记者进行研究并对他们进行问责。

sentences.en: Let's say there wasn't any of that.
sentences.zh: 假设根本没有这些。

sentences.en: So a year before the Paris Agreement was agreed to, in 2014, the global average temperature was on track to heat up by nearly four degrees Celsius by the end of this century.
sentences.zh: 因此，在《巴黎协定》达成的前一年，即2014年，全球平均气温正朝着在本世纪末升高近4摄氏度的方向发展。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Where are we now?
sentences.zh: 我们现在在哪里？

sentences.en: Well, we are on track to heat up by about three degrees Celsius.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们正朝着升温约3摄氏度的方向发展。

sentences.en: If all countries meet the targets that they've set for themselves, that could go down to about 2.4, 2.5 degrees of warming.
sentences.zh: 如果所有国家都达到他们为自己设定的目标，气温升幅可能会降至约2.4、2.5度。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Still bad, but you're saying not as bad as it could be.
sentences.zh: 仍然很糟糕，但你的意思是，没有原本可能那么糟。

sentences.en: As my colleagues wrote last week, where we're at is a better result.
sentences.zh: 正如我的同事上周所写的那样，我们目前的处境是一个更好的结果。

sentences.en: It's still devastating.
sentences.zh: 它仍然是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: So what's the lesson of that thought experiment?
sentences.zh: 那么这个思想实验的教训是什么？

sentences.en: So two lessons.
sentences.zh: 有两个教训。

sentences.en: First, that emissions can be reduced, that temperature rise can be limited.
sentences.zh: 首先，排放是可以减少的，温度上升是可以控制的。

sentences.en: And two, that perhaps this whole system, the way the Paris Accord is built around a system of diplomatic peer pressure
sentences.zh: 第二，也许整个系统，《巴黎协定》所围绕的这种基于外交同伴压力的系统，

sentences.en: around which the Paris Agreement is built, can deliver some results.
sentences.zh: 即构建《巴黎协定》的体系，能够取得一些成果。

sentences.en: And that is the whole point of why an international climate summit like this is taking place.
sentences.zh: 这就是举行这样一场国际气候峰会的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So to return to me to the question we started with, what is the value of a conference like this at this extremely dire stage in our climate history?
sentences.zh: 那么回到我最初的问题，在我们气候历史如此严峻的阶段，这样一场会议的价值是什么？

sentences.en: It sounds like what you're saying is that this self-evidently imperfect system is a system that does accomplish something.
sentences.zh: 听起来你的意思是，这个不言而喻的不完美系统是一个确实能取得一些成果的系统。

sentences.en: It's clearly not working as well as everyone would like, but it's better than the alternative,
sentences.zh: 它显然没有达到每个人期望的那么好，但它总比替代方案要好，

sentences.en: which is leaving every country to their own devices and hoping that they do the right thing for the climate on their own.
sentences.zh: 即任由每个国家我行我素，并希望它们自己为气候做正确的事情。

sentences.en: Is that the thinking?
sentences.zh: 这就是这种想法吗？

sentences.en: Well, look, what I can tell you is that this is a fundamentally global problem that no leader on its own is in a position to address.
sentences.zh: 好吧，听着，我能告诉你的是，这是一个根本上的全球性问题，没有任何一个领导人能够单枪匹马地解决。

sentences.en: So it needs, at its core, global collective action.
sentences.zh: 因此，其核心需要全球集体行动。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: A conference like this, a summit like this, is the first step in nudging countries, particularly big polluting countries, to do better.
sentences.zh: 像这样的一次会议、这样的一次峰会，是敦促各国（特别是污染大国）做得更好的第一步。

sentences.en: The second and most important step is to see if they will, to hold them accountable.
sentences.zh: 第二也是最重要的一步，是看他们是否会这样做，并追究他们的责任。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: For which, no doubt, we need another conference.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，为此我们需要又一次会议。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There will be another climate conference, and I will be covering it.
sentences.zh: 还将有另一次气候会议，我会进行报道。

sentences.en: Well, Simini, good luck.
sentences.zh: 好吧，西米尼，祝你好运。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们不胜感激。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: Virginia, we won this thing!
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚，我们赢了！

sentences.en: In the first major elections of the Biden presidency, the Republican candidate for governor of Virginia, Glenn Youngkin, has defeated his Democratic rival, Terry McAuliffe.
sentences.zh: 在拜登总统任内的首场重大选举中，弗吉尼亚州长共和党候选人格伦·扬金击败了他的民主党对手特里·麦考利夫。

sentences.en: Together, together, together, we will change the trajectory of this commonwealth.
sentences.zh: 齐心协力，我们将改变这个联邦的发展轨迹。

sentences.en: It was a major setback for Democrats in a state that Biden won last year by 10 points.
sentences.zh: 对于民主党人来说，这是一个重大挫折，因为拜登去年在该州以10个百分点的优势获胜。

sentences.en: In the race for governor of New Jersey, the contest between Republican Jack Cittarelli and his Democratic opponent, incumbent Governor Phil Murphy, remained too close to call.
sentences.zh: 在新泽西州州长竞选中，共和党人杰克·奇塔雷利与民主党对手、现任州长菲尔·墨菲之间的较量依然难分胜负。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, in Boston, Michelle Wu was elected mayor in a nonpartisan election, becoming the first woman and first person of color to lead that city.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在波士顿，米歇尔·吴在无党派选举中当选市长，成为领导该市的第一位女性和第一位有色人种。

sentences.en: And finally…
sentences.zh: 最后……

sentences.en: Tonight, New York has chosen one of you, one of our own.
sentences.zh: 今晚，纽约选择你们中的一员，我们自己人中的一员。

sentences.en: I am you.
sentences.zh: 我就是你们。

sentences.en: I am you.
sentences.zh: 我就是你们。

sentences.en: In New York City, as expected, the Democratic candidate for mayor, Eric Adams, soundly defeated his Republican rival.
sentences.zh: 在纽约市，正如预期的那样，民主党市长候选人埃里克·亚当斯大胜他的共和党对手。

sentences.en: Adams, a former New York City police officer, will become the city's second black mayor.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯曾是一名纽约市警官，将成为该市第二位黑人市长。

sentences.en: After years of praying and hoping and struggling and working, we're headed to City Hall.
sentences.zh: 经过多年的祈祷、希望、挣扎和奋斗，我们要前往市政厅了。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Mooj Zadie, Claire Tennesketter, Michael Simon-Johnson, and Rob Zipko.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由穆杰·扎迪、克莱尔·特内斯克特、迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊和罗布·齐普科制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow, Patricia Willens, and M.J.
sentences.zh: 由丽莎·周、帕特里夏·维伦斯和M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn, and engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩剪辑，克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: Original music by Marian Lozano.
sentences.zh: 原创音乐由玛丽安·洛萨诺创作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderland.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由奇境乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了群自称是改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的权斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我萨拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
